ac:layout-cell.p: Terminology follows the shared e-invoicing glossary. Local terms explain this feature; exact technical IDs, fields and source codes keep their stated meanings.

An exchange action is one separately tracked action to deliver an invoice, submit a public copy, or report an invoice event. Each action has its own result. For example, invoice delivery can succeed while public-copy submission still needs attention.

Part 1 explains the scope, people involved, workflow and open decisions. Start here for a stakeholder review. Part 2 gives the detailed behaviour and rules. Part 3 describes service interactions and data. Part 4 links requirements to the checks and evidence needed before release.

The design remains a draft. Confirmed means supported by the cited source, within its stated limits. Proposed choices still need review. Open decisions still need an owner’s recorded answer. Out of scope identifies work excluded from this proposal or handled by another feature. Service names describe logical responsibilities; they do not establish deployed services or approved API endpoints. Technical IDs and state names are kept so engineering, testing and stakeholders can refer to the same item.

This proposed logical design gives Sage services a controlled way to call Spain’s public platform (SPFE), operated by AEAT. The connector handles the platform’s communication protocol. It is separate from invoice retrieval and recipient lookup.

For each call, it checks the customer, represented legal entity, permitted action and environment. It selects an approved contract and credentials for that purpose, then performs only an enabled operation. It saves the request and response evidence and returns a result that clearly says whether the outcome is known, pending or unknown. The service that requested the call decides what that result means for its feature.
The supplied PRD describes the wider integration. The capability mapping below shows how this connector supports it and where related services retain responsibility.

PRD-SEI-214, FR2–6/19–23/27, separates connections, registration, capability readiness and routes. PRD-SEI-105, FR1–18, owns environment isolation. PRD-SEI-211 and PRD-SEI-212 supply retrieval and submission safety requirements. These are canonical product requirements, not evidence of a deployed public adapter.

ac:layout-cell.h3: Shared foundation and public protocol boundary
ac:layout-cell.p: The shared connectivity and routing spec owns the shared connection/profile qualification and route context across customer-provider integration and Sage platform interconnection. This connector remains the public-platform protocol and operation-evidence owner. It consumes a qualified connection/profile and owning feature action; it cannot activate a route, create invoice/reporting obligations or replace the shared route engine. Reuse public execution controls where proven, while checking exact role, represented-party authority, credential purpose and operation contract independently. Shared foundation reuse does not imply that public and private platforms expose the same interface.
ac:layout-cell.h3: How the connector supports the supplied PRD
ac:layout-cell.p: The PRD describes the full public-platform integration in the Sage Global e-Invoicing Platform. This spec describes the connector within that integration. The platform contains the shared invoicing capabilities; the Global API is the contract through which products and partners access them. The connector supports the business capabilities below without taking over invoice issuance, transformation or lifecycle decisions from their responsible services.

tr.td: Submit faithful invoice copies
Transmit the exact prepared file through a supported public operation. Save acknowledgement, rejection and error evidence separately from recipient delivery.

SPEC-SEI-007 owns the copy obligation and issuance trigger. SPEC-SEI-005/008 own qualified validation/transformation; SPEC-SEI-001 owns protected signing where required. Exact timing, UBL profile, metadata and attachment restrictions remain contract/country-rule checks.
Generate and store the Spain invoice identifier
Carry the approved identifier and preserve the supplied invoice identity in requests and responses. Do not invent its encoding.
The PRD lists supplier NIF, number, series and date. Format/Spain owners must confirm the final encoding and contract; invoice and records services own generation and storage.
Communicate invoice and payment status
Send an authorised report and save its independent response. Preserve raw external codes rather than assigning business meaning in the connector.

SPEC-SEI-009 owns actor authority, lifecycle interpretation and reporting rules. The PRD's Rejected, Fully Paid, Collected, Not Paid/Non-Payment and cancellation labels need an approved external mapping. Accepted applies only if the AEAT contract exposes it.
Retrieve invoices, messages and statuses
Execute supported discovery/read calls, including authorised status/payment queries, and return raw source responses within the correct entity scope. Distinguish an empty result from an outage.

SPEC-SEI-016 owns automated retrieval, source-file capture, covered progress and delivery to products; SPEC-SEI-009 owns status interpretation. Article 10 establishes status/payment consultation; GetRegisteredInvoice, GetInvoices and the two downloads now have supplied operation evidence. Exact filter/continuation/business shapes remain incomplete; no automatic public notification interface is supplied. Keep source correlation and observation time, distinguish status consultation from file download, and prevent duplicate business processing.
Authenticate and use credentials
Apply the selected AEAT authentication contract using protected credential references for the approved action and environment.
SPEC-SEI-001 owns credential custody and qualification. Customer certificate procurement remains out of scope. One accepted certificate does not establish authority for every operation.
Handle cancellation requests
Execute cancellation only where the confirmed contract supports the specific action and the responsible feature authorises it. Save request and result evidence.
PCN-Q01/Q03 must distinguish invoice cancellation, communication cancellation and cancellation of unsent local work. None automatically deletes an issued invoice or undoes an external effect.
Monitor, audit and recover failures
Record timestamps, acknowledgements, rejections, errors and retrieval activity. Detect uncertain outcomes and assign recovery to an owner.

Operations and feature owners agree service targets, retry safety, retention and support. Schema, authentication, duplicate/already-existing invoice, status and availability errors retain their actual source meaning.
Customer identity, authority and readiness
Onboarding and identity/authority services; connector checks effective evidence before each operation.
Certificate custody and purpose-specific use
Certificate management; connector receives protected references and results, not private keys.
Public discovery, polling, source archive and checkpoint
Receiving, retrieval and download; connector returns correlated source responses and files.
Issued invoice, validation, exchange plan and independent actions
Outbound and PRD-SEI-212; connector executes one approved public operation.
Status consultation and commercial/payment interpretation
Lifecycle; lifecycle requests source refresh and interprets the result; connector executes qualified public queries and preserves source observations without deriving buyer acceptance.
Recipient receiving destination
Recipient lookup; uses this connector only if an approved public lookup contract exists.

ac:layout-cell.p: The connector does not issue invoices, change customer routes, interpret absence of a private destination, create public-copy duties, own statutory archive retention, or provide a generic proxy to arbitrary URLs. Onboarding/registration mutations, if required by the final contract, remain owned by their feature service and must use this same operation-safety boundary.

tr.td: Legal entity / legal subject
The business to which the invoice or action belongs. Technical fields use legalSubject for this business.
Authority
Permission to perform a specific action for that business. Logging in or holding a certificate does not by itself give this permission.
Capability
A supported function, such as receiving invoices or signing them.
Route
The time-bound selection of platform and connection for a defined invoice scope and direction. A ready connection does not activate a route or rewrite earlier invoice plans.
Idempotency
Repeating the same logical request adds no effect within the contract’s defined scope and retention window. The contract binds request identity and input and defines conflict handling.
Reconciliation
Check the original operation against a reliable source to establish what actually happened before deciding the next action.
Gate
A condition, decision or evidence check that must pass before the next step can proceed.
Tenant
The customer account boundary used to keep one customer’s data and access separate from another’s.
Immutable / append-only
Immutable means a saved record cannot be changed. Append-only means later information is added as another record. Neither means indefinite retention.
Provenance
The record of where data came from and which versions, checks and changes produced the result.
Contract
The agreed inputs, outputs, behaviour and responsibilities between services or parties.
Durable
Saved through the agreed recovery boundary so the record survives a process restart or worker failure. Long-term retention is a separate policy.
Readiness

The current result of capability checks for a stated legal entity, actor, environment and route/profile, with evidence, limitations and a recheck condition. Readiness is separate from authority, route activation and invoice outcomes.
Public platform / SPFE / AEAT
SPFE is the Spain public e-invoicing platform. AEAT is the authority operating it. Each platform operation needs its own approved contract.
Connection / contract profile
Configuration for communication; the selected operation, protocol and schema, environment and safety rules. A connection does not activate a route.
Durable intent / execution claim
A saved request identity and fixed input before a possible external effect; permission for one worker to execute that work. An expired claim does not prove the earlier worker did nothing.
External effect / outcome unknown
A change in the public platform; a result for which that change may have happened but reliable evidence is missing. Check the original operation before repeating it.
Lease generation / version check
A number identifying the current worker’s claim; a check that a record still has the version expected by the caller. These prevent old workers or stale updates from replacing newer work.
Outbox / circuit breaker
A saved event waiting to be delivered; a control that temporarily stops calls after defined failures. Neither changes the invoice route.
Scope / evidence / cohort
The customer, legal entity, environment and action covered by a call; saved facts and references showing what happened; the group of consumers selected for activation.
Capability qualified
Exact operation, environment, contract and evidence are enabled for a defined cohort.
Every public function is supported or a customer route is active.
Known result
Correlated response/evidence durably recorded at its actual meaning.
Buyer acceptance, ERP consumption or completion of unrelated invoice exchange actions.
Pending
Work is saved and waiting for capacity, a response, local evidence recovery or owner action.
External success or invoice absence.
Outcome unknown
External effect may have happened; original operation must be reconciled.
Permission to create a fresh operation or switch environment.
Denied/unsupported
Scope, authority, capability or contract is insufficient; no new external effect is initiated.
Permanent business ineligibility.

ac:layout-cell.p: This is a Spain reference design. Reusable unchanged means the proposed design pattern can stay the same. Reusable with country binding means shared behaviour needs approved country rules or adapters. Country-specific rules stay in the Spain country pack. Unknown means that the existing implementation’s suitability or coverage still needs evidence. These labels do not prove production readiness. Another country needs its own assessment. See the shared e-invoicing glossary.

Step names describe the action in plain language. The smaller PCN references link each step to the detailed behaviour and acceptance checks below.

Text equivalent: Receive the service request (PCN-01) → Check customer and environment (PCN-02) → Check permission and credentials (PCN-03) → Check platform support (PCN-04) → Save the request before sending (PCN-05) → Call the public platform (PCN-06) → Save the response and evidence (PCN-07) → Return the result to the service (PCN-08). If permission is denied or the action is unsupported, hold the request without sending a call. If the external outcome is unknown or evidence is missing, check what happened before retrying (PCN-09), using the original request identity and context. Update settings for future requests (PCN-10) while preserving pending work and history.

tr.td: PCN-01 Receive the service request / owning feature service
Save a stable feature operation, input reference/digest and correlation.
Connector/feature: the same key with changed input returns a conflict.
PCN-02 Check customer and environment / connector
Resolve tenant, represented entity, country and environment from trusted records.
Identity/Security: deny ambiguous context before any access.
PCN-03 Check permission and credentials / connector and specialist services
Check current authority for the action and credentials for its purpose and environment.
Authority/Trust: missing or revoked permission holds new calls.
PCN-04 Check platform support / connector
Select the enabled operation, exact contract/version, retry-safety class and readiness evidence.
Integration owner: keep unsupported combinations disabled.
PCN-05 Save the request before sending / connector
Save the request and claim execution once, with fixed input and target context.
Connector/Records: a failed save prevents a new external change.
PCN-06 Call the public platform / adapter
Call within approved limits using the correct credential, contract and quota.
Adapter/Operations: record whether transmission may have happened. Check uncertain outcomes before repeat.
PCN-07 Save the response and evidence / connector
Save protected raw evidence, a safe normalised result and links to each item.
Records/connector: recover the original response without making a fresh external change.
PCN-08 Return the result to the service / connector
Return a result within scope and send a recoverable notification to the requesting feature.
Feature/connector: recognise repeated notifications and do not apply them twice.
PCN-09 Check what happened before retrying / operations or approved policy
Establish the original outcome, or keep an unresolved case with a responsible owner.
Operations/adapter: use manual recovery when safe query or retry is unproven.
PCN-10 Update settings for future requests / authorised integration owner
Record profile/group changes for future work, their impact and audit evidence.
Integration/Security: keep current work/history and other environments separate.

ac:layout-cell.p: Open decisions PCN-Q01–Q08 in Part 4 gate exact APIs, custody/authority, operation safety, evidence durability, service targets, deployment and rollout. A successful connection check is not blanket readiness. No live platform configuration is changed by this document.

Logical operation identity includes tenant, legal entity, country, environment, capability, owning feature operation and idempotency identity. Every attempt freezes contract profile, endpoint reference, credential binding, authority decision, payload digest and expected record version. Idempotency retention and scope must be agreed with each consumer/provider.

tr.td: PCN-I01
Trusted environment and credential binding must agree; production cannot fail over to simulation or TEST.
PCN-I02
Authentication, business authority, capability readiness, registration and route activation are separate facts.
PCN-I03
Only a qualified operation/profile may execute; one successful call does not qualify all capabilities.
PCN-I04
Same scoped key and digest returns/resumes the original operation; changed input conflicts.
PCN-I05
Save immutable intent before any possible external effect; uncertainty uses original identity and context.
PCN-I06
Successful transport or a successful request does not supply missing business results for individual items.
PCN-I07
Evidence and notification follow a recoverable commit; local save failure cannot justify fresh submission.
PCN-I08
Contract/credential changes keep historical context and apply only to eligible future work.
PCN-I09
Retry is controlled at one external execution owner; feature and connector retries cannot multiply public effects.
PCN-I10
Credentials, raw invoices and bearer access values never appear in client events or diagnostic logs.

ac:layout-cell.p: PCN-01 Accept the feature request. The calling Sage service asks the connector to perform a named platform action. Authenticate that service and check its permitted capability. Accept the feature operation reference, legal entity and action, fixed payload or query reference, digest and idempotency key. The caller cannot choose an arbitrary URL or protocol command.

Save a stable connector operation. A repeat with the same identity and input returns its current saved state. Changed input or context returns a conflict. A feature may cancel work before execution. Once an external change may have happened, cancellation cannot erase the history or claim that the change was undone.

PCN-02 Resolve the customer and environment. Check that the caller’s scope matches the connection’s legal entity, country and trusted deployment/account environment. Select the environment profile and approved destination from protected configuration. Reject missing, cross-tenant or conflicting context before accessing credentials.

Simulation uses clearly labelled synthetic test data. Official TEST access requires its confirmed contract. Neither simulation nor a TEST response proves production readiness or acceptance by the live public platform.

PCN-03 Check authority and credentials. Check local permission and external authority to act for the represented legal entity. Article 9/10 access uses its own registered-authority checks. Other actions use the authority rules approved for that action; one permission does not automatically cover another.

Obtain protected credential references through SPEC-SEI-001. Check purpose, environment, expiry/status and represented party under the current policy. If authority or credential versions change while the request waits, check again before execution. Hold new calls when required authority evidence is unavailable. A certificate alone cannot supply that authority, and the connector does not require private-key export.

PCN-04 Select the supported operation. Select an enabled registry entry for the requested action, country, environment and consumer group. It must identify the protocol and schema version, approved destination, request/response limits and response meaning. It must also identify possible external changes, provider idempotency/query support, timeout/retry rules and the evidence owner. Missing information blocks activation; do not borrow assumptions from another AEAT service. SII, VERI*FACTU and FACe contracts do not prove SPFE support.

Use approved readiness checks that do not change external state, or conformance evidence for the selected contract. Never send a real or empty invoice to test a connection. DNS/TLS/network checks show only that communication is possible. Show configuration, authentication/authority, operation support and current service health separately. Registration remains UNKNOWN/NOT_APPLICABLE unless the confirmed operating model provides a registration fact. A successful ping does not establish enrolment, and this design does not invent an enrolment endpoint.

PCN-05 Save the request and assign one worker. Save the operation, fixed input reference, exact scope/profile, feature correlation and retry-safety class. One execution owner claims the work through a numbered lease or equivalent concurrency control. A stale worker cannot save a result or initiate another attempt. Before sending, save the attempt identity and the point at which transmission may begin. Save queue work and operation records through a recoverable outbox or equivalent protocol. Missing payload, object or hash prevents execution.

An expired lease does not prove that the previous worker stopped transmitting. If a worker loses its lease or another worker takes over after a possible external effect, hold the original operation for reconciliation or a provider-proven idempotent resume. Do not start another change just because the local lease expired. Test claim checks immediately before transmission, rejection of stale saves and external retry safety together.

Combine only identical operations under the approved consumer contract. Limit queued work and share capacity fairly across tenants and capabilities. Submission backlog must not prevent retrieval or reconciliation. Exact quotas and priorities remain PCN-Q05 decisions.

PCN-06 Call the public platform. Build the request from the qualified contract and the checked feature request. Enforce resource limits, verify the remote transport identity, handle XML safely and use only approved destinations. Redirects or returned URLs cannot bypass destination or credential rules. The connector must not change signed invoice bytes or repair invoice facts.

Record whether failure happened before transmission, after possible transmission or after a response matched to the request. A call proven to have no external effect may repeat under its approved read/retry contract; “consult” in its name is not proof. A lost response after a possible change becomes OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. Throttling or an outage must not appear as an empty result or successful freshness check. A circuit breaker pauses affected calls; it does not switch route, environment or invoice exchange action. Exact waits and limits remain open.

PCN-07 Save response evidence. Save the protected response bytes or reference, digest, received time, external request/item references, contract/error catalogue version and what the response proves. Match each item result to the request. Keep partial or missing results visible; request-level success does not mean every item was admitted. Preserve unknown external error codes in restricted evidence and notify the catalogue owner. The caller receives a safe category and responsible owner.

Before temporary streamed files expire, obtain confirmation that the responsible service saved and verified them. SPEC-SEI-016 owns permanent invoice capture; connector staging is temporary. If the external result is known but saving its evidence fails, hold the operation for evidence recovery. Recover the original response or query the original operation instead of repeating a change. The implementation must prove that this recovery survives worker loss.

This is the shared SPFE response reference for PCN-07. It must capture every distinct response/error code found in the reviewed source set and supplied observations. Source meanings apply only to the stated operation and evidence version. Handling and owner columns are proposed Sage controls. The business and technical mapping covers all 600 active entries in SPFE-S28/S29 and preserves their parameters and duplicate definitions. Operation, response-field and runtime template bindings remain unqualified; source conflicts stay open. This matrix is not a complete wire-code catalogue or proof of support by another operation. REF-SPFE-EX09/REF-SPFE-OBS01; SPFE-Q20 — source coverage and catalogue qualification.

ac:layout-cell.p: For each code, record the operation, response level, exact XML field/namespace, original code and description, source/version, invoice or request correlation, field locations when supplied, proposed handling, owner and acceptance reference. Record unknown values explicitly. Add a separate binding when the same code occurs in another operation or source version; retain earlier meanings and flag conflicts. Do not invent unobserved codes from a numeric sequence or prefix. A new code is captured before its customer wording, retry policy or implementation support is qualified.

ac:layout-cell.p: The eight lifecycle communication codes remain authoritative in RES-SEI-002 — raw event codes and SPEC029's event contract. Query/download action values identify requests; they are not response statuses. Resource coverage and remaining operation-binding findings are recorded under SPFE-Q20.

SPEC005 UV-05 — validation correction handling owns validation consequences. Sending, retrieval and lifecycle use this matrix only for qualified operation bindings. Unknown codes retain their exact value and source under PCN-07; retry selection remains PCN-09 and cannot be inferred from a prefix or number. France processing errors and lifecycle reason codes are separate namespaces.

The customer needs an owned next action when an invoice check or SPFE call fails. Preserve the business or technical classification from the original file, then select proposed handling from the actual message and operation evidence. A business-file error can require an administrator or technical investigation. A technical-file error can identify a reference or search field that needs correction. SPFE-S28/S29.

The complete error mapping is the row-level catalogue for this section. It contains 513 business entries (512 distinct keys) and 87 technical entries (83 distinct keys). Each row retains source ID, line, exact property key, Spanish template, placeholders, source issues, handling group and open gates. Group definitions give the proposed owner, English customer wording, next action and repeat condition. Counts below include duplicate occurrences. Commented properties are excluded from active coverage and preserved separately.

tr.th: Proposed responsible owner and next action

Check the reported party, identity scheme or address. Keep invoice-party and caller identity separate.

Operation and message contract
Integration checks action/service compatibility. Do not change the business action to bypass the error.

Integration/Format checks schema diagnostics and document type. Assess generation or DTS mapping when Sage produced the XML.

ac:layout-cell.p: The mapping is a proposed design, not a deployed API contract. Its handling-group names are not API enums. Sage API error codes, severity, HTTP status, response field and operation remain unassigned for resource-only rows. A numeric property key is not an HTTP status. A technical category does not grant retry permission. PCN-09 owns repeat decisions from the original outcome and the qualified contract. An error does not create a buyer rejection, payment fact or lifecycle transition.

Preserve one catalogue identity per source ID + line, plus the file hash. Do not strip RULE_, remove suffixes, normalise zero-padding or use a key-only dictionary that drops duplicates. In particular, the four RULE_SPFE-CORE-18_MENSAJE_* messages describe different checks. The five RULE_SPFE-REPR-01_MENSAJE_* messages include a failed check, missing invoice, denied queries and unknown action. They cannot share one fixed customer message. The catalogue's observed_response_correspondences links the five existing response observations to candidate templates without converting semantic similarity into a runtime binding.

Explicit BT/BG mentions have path candidates from SPFE-S30/S31. A missing dictionary key remains unresolved. A path lookup is not a validated payload location or executable XPath; it does not supply missing message parameters. Keep SPFE-Q21 rule-ID/date conflicts open and retain the source's original wording.

Use the shared issue presentation, correlation and recovery pattern where qualified. Assess existing DTS first when generated XML or a field mapping caused the failure. Actual build, input/output contracts, Spain mappings, rule packs and operations still need evidence. Select these resources only for the qualified Spain country profile; France errors and other countries' rules remain separate. PCN-SPFE-A07–A09 define the acceptance coverage.

PCN-08 Return the result and notify the feature. The service that requested the call can read the saved result within its authorised scope. Notifications include connector/feature IDs, event ID, version, known/pending/unknown state and safe evidence references. A notification may arrive more than once or out of order, so consumers check identity and version before applying it.

The feature service decides what admission, freshness, retrieval progress, lifecycle status and customer wording mean. The connector cannot advance a retrieval checkpoint or mark the buyer as having accepted an invoice.

PCN-09 Establish the original outcome before retry. One recovery owner selects SAFE_RETRY, IDEMPOTENT_RESUME, RECONCILE_FIRST or MANUAL_ONLY from evidence about the operation. Do not choose from the error name alone. Query the original operation/reference with its payload digest, contract and environment. A failed query leaves the outcome unknown. Repeat only when the approved contract and evidence of non-execution permit it.

Changing a route or credential does not resolve an earlier outcome. A replacement credential needs an approved link to the original represented party, action and environment, with evidence for the new attempt. If neither reliable query nor proven idempotency is available, open a manual case with an owner and hold unsafe repeats. Reusing the same local key cannot bypass that hold.

Inspection, recovery and profile activation require separate audited permissions. Cancellation after transmission is a separate external operation, if supported by a qualified contract, and remains the feature service’s responsibility.

PCN-10 Change configuration safely. Check that the current profile/endpoint version matches the expected version before applying a change. Record the actor, reason, impact and approval evidence. Deploy the capability disabled, obtain correctly labelled TEST/simulation evidence, then enable only the approved production group.

Credential rotation keeps earlier attempts unchanged. Disablement stops new affected calls and assesses queued work, work already running and unresolved operations. Keep their evidence and leave other capabilities/environments separate. Rollback restores a qualified profile for eligible future work; it must not repeat completed or outcome-unknown operations.

Enforce trusted tenant/entity/country/environment and qualified credential binding before calls; PRD105 FR1–9/14/17, PRD214 FR6.

PCN-R08

PCN-R09
Preserve in-flight/history through credential/profile change, suspension and rollback; PRD105 FR15–16, PRD214 FR16–18/25–26.

ac:layout-cell.p: Encryption, least privilege and purpose-bound source access protect PCN-D01–D09. Metrics distinguish attempts before/after transmission, provider and local latency, throttle, authority denial, evidence gaps, unknown-operation age and notification backlog. Avoid legal-subject identifiers as public metric labels. Security owns destination restrictions and XML/resource limits; Operations/Product approve service objectives from provider terms and measured volumes. No numeric SLA or retention period is invented.

Assess existing sending calls; qualify Spain payloads and separate delivery/copy results.

ac:layout-cell.p: One Sage request can coordinate several external calls. Product reads can use saved evidence; a required source refresh uses a qualified connector query. The connector preserves each operation result; the owning feature applies its business meaning. DocumentStatus is a response-document type, so apply the SPFE response and error matrix to distinguish query, validation and reporting results from invoice lifecycle facts.

For direct Sage-to-SPFE work, this connector executes the assigned operation. Provider-owned actions retain their execution owner; apply SPEC-SEI-013's integration-mode ownership rules to prevent duplicate execution. The public connector role is separate from Sage's private-platform operator role. REF-API-MAP.

ac:layout-cell.h2: Part 3 Logical Service Interactions and Data Inventory
ac:layout-cell.p: These are logical operations, not endpoint names. Commands carry requestId, connector/feature operation IDs, trusted scope, capability, contractProfileRef, payload/query reference and digest, idempotency key, correlation and expectedVersion as appropriate. Protected values stay references. Responses distinguish known outcome, pending work, denial, unsupported capability, conflict, temporary failure, outcome unknown and evidence-recovery hold.

tr.td: PCN-D01 Connection/capability profile / registry

Stable connection, country/environment, operation/protocol and schema, governed destination, activation/cohort, read/mutation semantics, idempotency/query rules, limits, source/effective version; restricted/versioned.
PCN-D02 Eligibility snapshot / authority/trust owners
Entity/action, actor/workload, policy/authority and credential references, principal/environment/purpose, validity/check time; restricted/append-only evidence. No credentials copied.
PCN-D03 Operation intent / connector
Scoped key, feature/connector IDs, digest, immutable payload/query reference, safety class, cancellation and current operation version; restricted, immutable input.
PCN-D04 Execution attempt / connector
Attempt/lease generation, fixed profile/destination/bindings, pre/post-transmission markers, correlation/times and safe result; append-only.
PCN-D05 External response / connector + Records
Raw protected reference/hash, per-item correlations, external codes/references, observed state and evidence meaning, catalogue version; sensitive/immutable.
PCN-D06 File handoff / connector + Records
Temporary source/reference/hash/expiry, durable capture receipt and owner; sensitive, bounded staging. Permanent archive belongs to feature/Records.
PCN-D07 Recovery case / Operations
Original operation, reason/safety, evidence/last query, owner, approved next action and escalation; restricted/versioned.
PCN-D08 Notification outbox / connector
Event ID, operation/result version, target owner, delivery attempts/receipt and evidence refs; restricted/replayable.
PCN-D09 Action audit / audit owner
Actor, scope/action/reason/time, versions and before/after state, evidence references and retention/hold class; restricted/append-only.

ac:layout-cell.p: The public platform is authoritative for its external results; connector records are authoritative for Sage intent/attempts. Feature services own business interpretation. Retention, idempotency windows, evidence holds and staging expiry are PCN-Q04 decisions by data class; connector cleanup cannot dispose of a feature's archived invoice or unresolved-case evidence.

Assess existing Sage public transport, credential access, operation/outbox and monitoring capabilities. Record source build/design pattern, retained behaviour, Spain changes, missing operations, accountable owner and qualification evidence. The same adapter library, gateway or service deployment are alternative physical choices under PCN-Q06; whichever is selected must have one execution/idempotency owner and durable recovery. Capability selection must not copy Spain authority, error or routing rules into another country. No DTS transformation is introduced in this contract.
These scenarios specify evidence to obtain; they are not executed implementation tests.

tr.td: PCN-A01 Wrong tenant/environment or untrusted override
Denial before credential/public access; no production-to-TEST fallback.
PCN-A02 Valid certificate, missing/revoked action authority
New call held; represented subject/action evidenced; other grants not inferred.
PCN-A03 Network check succeeds, operation unqualified
Capability stays unsupported; no invoice probe or route activation.
PCN-A04 Duplicate and changed intent
Same key/digest resumes original; changed context conflicts; concurrent workers produce one effective execution claim.
PCN-A05 Pre-send failure versus lost response
Proven pre-send retry permitted; possible effect becomes unknown and reconciles original operation.
PCN-A06 No reliable query/idempotency contract
Manual-only hold; repeated feature request cannot bypass it.
PCN-A07 Partial response/unknown error
Missing items remain unresolved; protected source code retained; safe message does not claim blanket admission.
PCN-A08 External success, local persistence failure
Original outcome/evidence reconstructed without fresh mutation; crash evidence proves recovery.
PCN-A09 Capture/notification delayed
Temporary file durably handed off before expiry; repeated/out-of-order events do not regress consumer state.
PCN-A10 Throttle/outage and competing tenants
Bounded fair backlog and circuit breaker with approved rules; no false empty result, freshness or route switch.
PCN-A11 Rotation/disablement/rollback during work
Original context preserved; stale worker rejected; replacement authority checked; unaffected cohorts continue.
PCN-A12 Unsafe content/destination and support access
XML/resource and destination controls enforced; no credentials/raw bodies in errors/logs; unauthorised recovery denied.
PCN-A13 Country isolation and reuse qualification
Selected build/contracts proved; missing country binding blocks activation; Spain authority/error rules do not affect another country.
PCN-A14 Shared foundation handoff
Public operations consume the qualified role/profile and original action, retain one execution owner and cannot activate routes or inherit private-interface readiness.

Blocks conformance; preserve external semantics, source hashes and durable capture/result receipts. ac:layout-cell.p: Design review: agree boundaries and PCN-Q01–Q04/06/07, leaving unavailable interfaces explicit. Pilot: activate only qualified operations and exercise A01–A13 against the selected test contract and owning features. Production: resolve Q05/Q08, custody/retention and outstanding action-specific contracts; require conformance, security, crash/recovery evidence and measured support objectives. This is a reviewable logical proposal, not an approved design or live connector deployment.

Use the original files for the claims they establish. Final published regulation governs legal requirements; technical files supply their stated contract facts. Examples are illustrative. Missing or conflicting evidence remains a named gate. Product requirements and Sage design controls have separate authority. The English guide and extracts are reading aids.
